page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the Intel Xeon platform. Configured with 48 physical cores and 96 virtual cores across an x86_64 architecture, this instance operates with dedicated hyperthreaded CPU cores, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache. It features support for instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512F. The instance includes 86.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, requiring networked block storage, and it includes no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data demonstrates a clear contrast between single-threaded and parallel processing throughput. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution registers in the bottom quartile, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression similarly reflect legacy per-core clock constraints. However, multi-core scaling yields strong aggregate performance, placing stress-ng multi-core metrics in the top 25 percent. The instance also shows exceptional read bandwidth, exceeding 3900 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 190 GB/sec for larger blocks, enabling high-throughput operations such as Redis SET benchmarks at 63.93 million operations per second.

The compute-skewed hardware profile presents specific efficiency tradeoffs. With less than 1 GB of memory per core, it offers high parallelism without the financial overhead of large, unutilized memory footprints. Workloads reliant on single-thread frequency or expansive in-memory state will face bottlenecks. Consequently, the instance is well suited for highly parallel batch processing, distributed compilation, stateless microservice scaling, and CPU-driven vector mathematics that benefit from AVX-512 extensions.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused instance configured with 96 vCPUs from 48 physical Intel Xeon cores on the x86_64 architecture and 86.0 GB of system memory. Lacking integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, the instance provides approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU, targeting workloads that require dense multi-threaded computation without excessive memory provisioning. Benchmark results show modest single-thread capability alongside strong multi-core scaling and high memory read throughput, registering top-quartile performance in stress-ng multi-threaded tests and Redis operations. The resource ratio makes this instance appropriate for parallel compute workloads, Clang code compilation, distributed microservices, and compute-heavy batch tasks.
